learning_outcomes.text: Interpret and/or elaborate the necessary information for the correct development of a manufacturing process.
Develop Numerical Control programs based on the input documentation to the system.
Analyze the economic aspects associated with manufacturing to select optimal conditions, considering technological and socioeconomic aspects.
Apply advanced concepts related to product verification and inspection from a quality control perspective.

syllabus_topics: Systems and information necessary for manufacturing
Parameters related to processes and Economic aspects
Formulation of time and cost functions
Materialization of units and verification of forms
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as (0.75 * E) + (0.25 * PL). E evaluates theoretical-practical knowledge from expository classes and classroom practices via a single written exam. PL assesses practical laboratory knowledge through continuous in-person evaluation. No minimum mark is required for either component. For differentiated evaluation, a single written exam covers both theoretical-practical (E) and laboratory (PL) contents with the same weighting. The faculty may request an in-person defense if there is doubt about the authorship of an evaluable test or the use of unauthorized means.
